anchor.title: Smiles instinctively; this usually happens randomly, especially while sleeping.

items.title: Looks in the direction of a noise.
Looks at the person speaking to them.
Keeps their head stable but still requires support when carried in an upright position.
Can look at an object or person at arm's length.
Extends arms and legs when lying on their tummy.
Turns their head both ways when held upright.
Lying on their back, they lift their head and make an effort to sit up.
Sits upright and steady when leaning on pillows or furniture.
Tries to sit up when lying on their back while you pull them up by the hands.
Grabs a small object placed in their hands.
When lying on their tummy, they lift their head for a short time.

anchor.title: Brings their hands to their mouth.

items.title: Turns their head to follow objects with their eyes.
Watches curiously and intently while you do things.
Listens to people talking.
Stays focused on something or someone for a while (1 minute).
Chooses to pay attention to a person or situation.
Pays attention to new places and things.
Becomes aware of their surroundings.
Acts interested in unfamiliar things around them by exploring.

anchor.title: Uses different tones in their babbling.

items.title: Makes guttural sounds, like 'ga' or 'gu'.
Makes vowel sounds like 'eh' or 'ah'.
Moves their arms around when they see something they like.
Lets likes and dislikes be known by making facial expressions.
Uses sounds like 'm, n, p, t, d' when babbling.

anchor.title: Reacts when they see themselves in a mirror.

items.title: Responds positively to loving gestures.
Recognizes caregivers.
Stares at the person who is talking to them.
Smiles when people make eye contact.
Reacts to different tones of voice.
Stares at people's faces.
Becomes calm when hearing voices they know.
Acts differently when around familiar and unfamiliar adults.

calibration.title: Points to a red object when you ask.
